public_rationale: The claim is conditional. If someone carefully builds the comprehension challenge Marcus described, no system available around April 2025 would come close to human performance. He gave no deadline. The contract scores the claim only after a test meeting his design conditions is published with human and April-2025-era system results. The evidence packet contains no such test as of 2026-10-28. The only evidence item is LVBench, a long-video benchmark paper available 2025-10-20 (e1). It reports human accuracy of 94.4% on average. Gemini-2.5-Pro scored 67.4% and Seed1.5-VL scored 64.0%. That gap points the same way as the claim. But LVBench uses multiple-choice questions. Per e1, it is not refreshed against contamination and lacks the other design features in his condition. So it does not meet the antecedent, and the forecast stays unresolved.
limitations: The evidence does not show that any test meeting the stated conditions exists: full shows, refreshed questions, careful scoring and secure first-time-viewer conditions.
LVBench results do not show how systems would perform on open-ended explanation questions.
The contract sets no numeric threshold for 'come close', so how a future result is read will depend on interpretation.
The search may have missed a recent or obscure implementation of the challenge.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: If a careful comprehension challenge test were built, no current AI system would come close to human performance on it.
conditions: if someone carefully built out the comprehension challenge test

statement.excerpt: But I am willing to wager that if someone put in that kind of effort and carefully built out the test, no current system would come close to human performance.
statement.document_title: AI has (sort of) passed the Turing Test; here’s why that hardly matters

from_speaker: if someone put in that kind of effort
would come close to human performance
our_interpretation: The condition is that someone builds the comprehension challenge he describes: a well-funded ($25-50M scale) test where systems watch full TV shows or films and answer questions. The questions are refreshed to avoid contamination, answers are scored carefully (perhaps by hand), and the machine is kept on the same footing as a first-time human viewer.
'Current system' means AI systems available around the post date, 2025-04-02.
'Not come close' means a large gap between the best such system and human viewers.
criteria.support_condition: A test meeting the condition is built, and systems from around April 2025 score far below human viewers on it.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A test meeting the condition is built, and a system from around April 2025 scores at or near human level on it.
